Tidy Summaries of nbreg and zinbreg Fits

Source: R/tidiers.R
tidiers-nbzinbreg.Rd

tidy() returns a data frame with one row per parameter (estimate, standard error, z statistic, p-value, and optionally a confidence interval); for zinbreg fits a component column marks the count and zero parts. glance() returns a one-row data frame of model-level statistics (log-likelihood, AIC, BIC, theta, number of observations, convergence). Both are convenient for building tables in reports.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An nbreg or zinbreg fit.

conf.int

Logical; add Wald confidence limits (conf.low, conf.high) to the tidy() output.

conf.level

Confidence level for conf.int = TRUE.

...

Not used (an error if supplied).

Value

tidy(): a data frame with one row per coefficient and columns term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value (and conf.low, conf.high), plus component for zinbreg. glance(): a one-row data frame with logLik, AIC, BIC, theta, SE.theta, nobs, df, df.residual, iter and converged, plus newton_decrement for zinbreg.

Details

tidy() gives the same estimates, standard errors, z statistics and p-values as the coefficient tables of summary(). With conf.int = TRUE it adds Wald limits from confint() (NA for coefficients without a finite estimate). theta is a model-level quantity and appears in glance(), not as a tidy() row (for zinbreg, the Log(theta) row of the summary() count table is left out).

For zinbreg fits, tidy() has a component column ("count" or "zero"), and term is the coefficient name within its part, as in coef(fit, model = "count"). glance() adds newton_decrement, the gradient check at the estimates.

Errors and warnings

nbzinbreg_error_input: x of the wrong class, conf.int not TRUE or FALSE, conf.level outside (0, 1), or unused arguments.

See also

generics::tidy(), generics::glance()

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:8, y = c(1, 0, 6, 1, 9, 2, 20, 4))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
#>          term   estimate std.error  statistic    p.value    conf.low conf.high
#> 1 (Intercept) -0.1133373 0.8415831 -0.1346715 0.89287157 -1.76280995 1.5361353
#> 2           x  0.3439702 0.1545082  2.2262266 0.02599901  0.04113975 0.6468007
glance(fit)
#>      logLik      AIC     BIC    theta SE.theta nobs df df.residual iter
#> 1 -20.34479 46.68958 46.9279 1.509052 1.025461    8  3           6    4
#>   converged
#> 1      TRUE
if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  zfit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                  data = bioChemists)
  tidy(zfit)
  glance(zfit)
}
#>      logLik      AIC      BIC    theta SE.theta nobs df df.residual iter
#> 1 -1553.271 3124.542 3167.913 2.726166 0.389377  915  9         906  126
#>   converged newton_decrement
#> 1      TRUE     9.354037e-09
